I work for an American airline.
I manage thirty corporate accounts.
This year the company is rolling out a regional structure.
At the moment I am spending more time with clients than in the office.
Rosa? Diego Restrepo, from the Bogotá office. We are on the same call on Thursday, so I thought I would say hello first.
Hello, Diego. Thank you for calling. I am Rosa, and I am in charge of the corporate accounts in São Paulo.
Corporate only? How big is your client portfolio?
About thirty companies. Most of them are banks and technology companies, and I visit two or three of them every week.
That is a serious workload. Mine is smaller, but I also cover Ecuador, so I am on a plane most weeks.
Then we have the same life. And this year my team is rolling out the new structure, so nothing is quiet.
Nothing is quiet anywhere. Are you coming to the convention in November? Everybody from the four countries is going.
I am. It will be good to put faces to the names. And you — how long have people in Bogotá worked with one regional office?
I am an account manager in the commercial area.
I am in charge of the corporate clients in Sao Paulo.
My client portfolio covers about thirty companies.
This year we are rolling out a new regional structure.
Could you say that again, a little more slowly?

Rosa, hi, it is Paulo from the regional program office. I am calling about the kick-off call on Thursday. It moved from ten to eleven in the morning, Sao Paulo time, because the Santiago team asked for it. The call runs for fifty minutes and there are eleven of us on it, and it is all in English. You do not need to prepare a presentation. What we do need from every account manager is one minute at the start: your name, your city, and what your portfolio looks like today. That is it. I am sending the invitation this afternoon. Call me back if Thursday does not work for you.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the first commercial update of the new structure. Let me start with what is changing and what is not. The commercial teams in Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Colombia now report into one regional office instead of four separate ones. That is the change. What is not changing is your client portfolio. Nobody is moving accounts this quarter. The second point is meetings. From September, we run one regional call a week, on Thursday mornings, and it replaces the four local calls you have today. And the third point, which matters most for the people in this room: the working language of the regional office is English. Not because anybody prefers it, but because eleven people from four countries need one language to share a call.

Diego introduces himself and explains that he is calling from the Bogota office. Rosa gives her name and says she is in charge of the corporate clients in Sao Paulo. Diego asks how big her client portfolio is, and Rosa answers with the number and the kind of company. Rosa explains that the commercial area is rolling out the new regional structure this year. Diego asks whether she is coming to the convention, and Rosa says she is, and asks him the same question back.
